instruction: SAFETY/BYPASS R1 review of WP-SCP-022 slice TF-020P-005 at branch feature/wp-scp-022-tf-020p-005-pre-push-verify, HEAD commit 7b29dbc. The slice introduces scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh as a local-dev wrapper. Verify the SAFETY surface exhaustively against the SCP threat model (the wrapper is INFORMATIONAL — CI is the authoritative gate — but it must not introduce any new bypass surface or weaken existing assumptions). Specifically: (1) Bypass-surface inventory: does the wrapper introduce any path where a developer could subvert CI's enforcement? Concrete attack paths to check: (a) tampered local opa/regal binary returns success while CI binary returns failure — does the wrapper claim authority over the result, or correctly disclaim it? (b) wrapper itself is tampered to silently skip a gate — does CODEOWNERS scripts/** @jrnb2024 cover it, and is the wrapper's PR-time review sufficient to detect tampering? (c) Could a developer install a shadow git rev-parse, find, or awk to subvert tool resolution? (Probably not realistic, but flag if obvious.) (2) Shell injection / quoting: review every variable expansion in scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh for unquoted use that could mishandle paths with spaces, newlines, or shell metacharacters. Specifically: (a) REPO_ROOT, POLICIES_DIR, TOOL_VERSIONS_FILE, COMMON_FILE, TEST_ROOT, rule_file, test_file, rule_base, test_name (b) the find -print0 / read -r -d '' pipeline (c) the awk invocation reading .tool-versions (d) the regal lint and opa test arg lists. Flag any quoting that could let a maliciously-named .rego file (e.g. policies/'; rm -rf /'.rego) escape into shell evaluation. (3) Threshold-90 silent-drop risk: verify the --coverage --threshold 90 --fail-on-empty -v flags are passed exactly as written — no shell variable expansion in the flag string (which would let an env var override the threshold). Confirm the literal '90' is in the script. (4) Repo-root escape: verify git rev-parse --show-toplevel handles the case where the user is in a worktree or submodule. Verify nothing in the script writes outside REPO_ROOT (no /tmp scratch files except those under user control; no symlink-following operations that could escape). (5) Tool-version drift safety: the version-parity warning is non-fatal by design. Is this the right choice? Argue both sides briefly. Does a developer running with regal 0.30.0 vs CI's 0.40.0 get a SILENTLY-DIFFERENT verdict than CI, leading to false confidence? If so, is the warning loud enough? (6) Concurrency: if two operators run the wrapper concurrently in the same checkout, do they interfere? (Probably no — but flag if any tempfile collision risk.) (7) Information disclosure: does the wrapper emit any sensitive content (env vars, paths from outside the repo, ssh keys) that a developer might paste into a bug report? (8) ADOPT-001 §12.7.9.1 amendment: does it correctly disclaim authority — i.e. CLEAR statement that 'CI is still the authoritative gate'? Or does it mislead adopters into believing local-pass = CI-pass? (9) Pre-existing assumption: the §12.7.9 (parent section) carries strong language about local clones needing to be at the same commit SHA as the wrapper pin. The new §12.7.9.1 wrapper is invoked from the SCP repo itself, not from an adopter clone — so the §12.7.9 SHA-pinning warning does NOT apply. Verify the §12.7.9.1 framing makes this distinction clearly OR adds an explicit 'this section is for SCP-repo rule authors, not adopter wrapper users' clarifier. If unclear, file an inline-fix. (10) Threat-model alignment: read docs/security/ briefly (or SECURITY.md) for the SCP threat model; verify the wrapper does not violate any documented invariant. NEVER recommend descoping; propose inline-fix or file as TF-020P-005a/b. Output to docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/020p-005-pre-push-verify/review-safety.json conforming to schemas/sonnet_review_result.schema.json.
